title: Equipment record
purpose: Review one piece of equipment: its details, limits, due dates, service events, recent LN2 entries and readings, excursions and status history, and reach the actions to record against it.
summary: One piece of equipment: details, limits, due dates, service events, recent LN2 entries and readings, excursions and status history.

tasks.title: Record maintenance or calibration
steps: Select [[Record service event]] and attach the certificate or report.

tasks.title: Record a reading or LN2 entry
steps: Select [[Record reading]] or [[Record LN2 entry]] in its section.

tasks.title: Take it out of service
steps: Managers and administrators: select [[Change status]] and give a reason.

tasks.title: Fix an entry recorded wrongly
steps: Select [[Correct]] on the entry. The original stays visible.

good_to_know: Limits and low levels are the values your repository set. The application sets none.
Corrections and withdrawals add an entry. Nothing is edited in place.
Anyone who can read the record can download its attachments.

sections.title: What the page shows
paragraphs: A table of contents at the top jumps to each section. The header shows the status, kind, storage unit, Critical equipment and location. When excursions are open or awaiting review a red notice says how many and links to them. Sections for LN2 entries appear only for LN2 tanks and supply dewars; sections for readings and excursions appear for everything except temperature monitors.
Retired equipment takes no new entries: the record buttons are disabled with a note, until a manager changes its status back to in service or out of service.

sections.title: Equipment and Limits
paragraphs: OpenBGA Biorepository has no default limits, refill levels or service intervals and never works out a due date: every one of them is entered by your repository, and what the page shows is what was entered. Each reading and excursion keeps the limits in force when it was recorded.

items.label: Equipment section
items.description: Asset ID, name, kind, status, whether it is critical, storage unit (linked), location, manufacturer and model, serial number, installed date, service provider, who registered it and when, and notes.

items.label: Lower limit, Upper limit
items.description: The temperature limits in °C, or No limit set.

items.label: Level unit, Low level
items.description: LN2 tanks and supply dewars only: the unit levels are read in and the level your repository refills at.

sections.title: Due dates
paragraphs: One row for each of maintenance, calibration, mapping and qualification. A row shows the next due date entered on the latest effective event of that kind. A later event without a next due date clears the date; a repair never has one. Nothing is calculated from an interval. Overdue means the date is before today, Due today is today, Scheduled is later. Days is the number of days from today, negative when overdue. Last performed links to the service event.

sections.title: Service events
paragraphs: The latest 200 events, newest first, with the count. Entries are never edited or deleted. A correction adds a new entry that replaces the values of the old one, or withdraws it, and it always needs a reason; the original stays visible in the log marked Corrected and the new one is marked Correction (or Withdrawal).

items.label: Performed, Service, Outcome
items.description: The date performed, the kind of event with its description under Description, and its outcome.

items.label: Performed by, Reference
items.description: The staff member or outside provider, and the certificate, work order or procedure reference with any reference device.

items.label: As found, As left, Next due
items.description: Calibration readings before and after, and the date your repository set for the next one.

items.label: Attachment
items.description: The certificate or report, downloaded as a file. Anyone who can read the record can download it.

items.label: Entry
items.description: Effective, Correction, Corrected or Withdrawal, with the correction reason, links between the old and new entry, and who recorded it and when.

items.label: Correct
items.description: Opens the correction form. Shown to the person who recorded the event and to managers and administrators, and not on an entry that was already corrected or withdrawn.

sections.title: LN2 log and Temperature readings
paragraphs: Each shows the latest 20 effective entries with a link to the full list for this equipment (All entries in the LN2 log, All readings). Record LN2 entry and Record reading open the forms with this equipment preselected. Each reading shows Above upper limit, Below lower limit, Within recorded limits or No limits recorded. The comparison uses the bounds saved with that reading. A value equal to a bound is within it. Change since previous is worked out from the levels and not entered.

sections.title: Excursions
paragraphs: Every excursion on this equipment, newest first, linked to its record. New excursion opens the form with this equipment preselected.

sections.title: Status history
paragraphs: Each status change with the time it took effect, the change, the reason, and who recorded it and when. Equipment registered and never changed shows In service since it was registered.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: The newest 50 recorded changes to this record (registration, edits, status changes, service events, entries and exports), shown oldest to newest with the person and the reason. It cannot be edited or deleted.

items.label: Edit
items.description: Managers and administrators. Opens the equipment form.

items.label: Change status
items.description: Managers and administrators. Opens the status form.

items.label: Record service event
items.description: Technicians, managers and administrators. Opens the service event form. Disabled with a note when the equipment is retired.

items.label: Record LN2 entry, Record reading, New excursion
items.description: Technicians, managers and administrators; in the LN2 log, Temperature readings and Excursions sections, hidden when the equipment is retired.
